notes: CLOSED 2026-08-30 by a native, axiom-free kernel construction (lane fermat-easy). `pow 2 (pow 2 n)` is `Even` for any `n` (`pow_pos` gives the exponent positive, `succ_pred_of_pos` rewrites it as `succ (pred _)`, making the power defeq `mul j 2` for `j := pow 2 (pred (pow 2 n))`, defeq `add (add 0 j) j`; `zero_add` plus `congr` land on the witness form `Even` needs), and `even_iff_odd_succ`'s `mp` direction turns that `Even` into `Odd (succ _)`, defeq `Odd (fermatNumber n)` since `add x 1` collapses via `add`'s right-recursion on the concrete `1`. Entirely symbolic: `n` stays free throughout, largest formed numeral is the base `2`. Reuses the private `odd_fermat_number_local`/`even_pow_two_of_pos` helpers already built for `coprime_fermatNumber_fermatNumber`'s proof (`fermat_number_mirrors.rs`), declared as its own theorem in `crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/nat_prelude/fermat_number_mirrors.rs::declare_odd_fermatnumber`. Verified symbolically (admitted over a genuinely free `n`) and at a concrete instance (`nat_prelude_tests.rs::fermat_number_easy_mirrors_apply_at_free_and_concrete_instances_with_two_negative_controls`, n=1: `Odd (fermatNumber 1) = Odd 5`, with a negative control confirming this is NOT defeq to `Even 5`).
